title: Permission to Run
subtitle: Across every store.
description: A worked hypothetical dealership handoff: a trade exception stalls a Friday deal. Name the approver, send the figures and measure the wait.
dek: A Friday-night deal waits on an unsigned trade exception. Put the approval limit and the handoff in writing before the next customer sits down.

ownership.title: Someone has to approve the $18,000.
paragraphs: The salesperson has promised more than the desk can approve. F&I is holding the worksheet. The GM has the authority, but the request hasn't told the GM what to decide.
Permission, people and patience become useful when the desk has a written dollar limit and an approver who answers. Give the rule a week of live deals, then fix the part that still holds customers.

rail: The deal, its times and its costs are invented for this example.
Set approval limits using your deal economics and record actual reply times.

scenario.title: Friday, 7:10 p.m.
scenario.label: Worked hypothetical · Every event and figure is invented
paragraphs: F&I receives a worksheet showing $18,000 for the customer's trade. The desk appraised it at $17,000. The salesperson has already quoted $18,000. Under this example's store rule, the desk manager can add $500 to the appraisal. The remaining $500 needs the GM's approval.

The GM is off-site. The desk sends a message: "Need you on a trade." It leaves out the figures. Approval arrives at 7:28. The desk corrects the worksheet, and F&I can resume at 7:34. The deal has waited 24 minutes.

cost.title: What the hold costs in this example
paragraphs: Assume every other deal figure stays fixed and the extra trade allowance comes out of expected gross profit. The $1,000 exception uses $1,000 of that gross. The delay also takes 24 minutes from the buyer and the staff. This example assigns no payroll cost or lost-sale value to those minutes.
cards: Assumed reduction in expected gross profit
Invented hold before F&I can resume

parts: Quote the approved trade figure. If a different figure has already been promised, tell the desk exactly what the customer heard.
Check the appraisal against the promised figure. Send the over-limit request to the named approver. Stay with the deal until F&I confirms receipt of the approved worksheet.
Approve the amount or return a figure the desk can take to the customer. Put the answer in writing. Name the backup before leaving the store.
Read back the approved trade figure when accepting the worksheet. Flag any mismatch before preparing the customer's final paperwork.

handoff.title: Send one message the GM can answer
handoff.label: Suggested script · Same hypothetical deal
handoff.intro: At 7:10, the desk manager could send this:
script: Trade appraisal: $17,000. Customer was quoted $18,000. My approval limit is $17,500.
Please approve $18,000 or return a figure I can take back to the customer. F&I has paused the worksheet. Please answer by 7:15. I'm staying with this deal.
handoff.reply: Approved at $18,000. I accept the $1,000 difference. Send F&I the revised worksheet with this approval.
handoff.followThrough: The desk sends both items together. F&I replies with the trade figure it received. The salesperson gives the customer the next update.

monday.title: Before Monday opening
paragraphs: Have the GM sign a short approval rule. In this example, the desk can approve up to $17,500 on a $17,000 appraisal. The GM or assigned backup approves anything higher. Your store should set its own dollar limits using its deal economics.

Put the backup's name and contact route beside the rule. If the trial reply deadline passes, the desk calls that person. Keep the request and the answer with the worksheet so the next person can see what was approved.

measures.title: Measure the wait next week
measures.label: Suggested trial targets · Actual results still need measuring
cards: Log when the desk sends a complete request and when approval or a revised figure arrives. Report the median wait and the longest wait.
Aim for every over-limit worksheet to carry its approval.
Record the share sent with written approval. Count returned worksheets once per deal; note each missing or conflicting trade figure.

basis: AVC worked hypothetical. All deal figures, times, approval limits and events are invented assumptions. The response and handoff targets are suggestions to test. No store results or industry statistics are presented.
transcript:
This is a hypothetical dealership deal. Every number and event is invented for this example.

At ten minutes past seven on Friday evening, finance and insurance receives a worksheet showing eighteen thousand dollars for a trade. The desk appraised the trade at seventeen thousand dollars. The salesperson has already quoted eighteen thousand dollars. Under this example's store rule, the desk can approve seventeen thousand five hundred dollars. The customer's quoted figure needs the general manager's approval.

The general manager is away. The desk asks for help with a trade, but leaves out the figures. The answer arrives eighteen minutes later. The revised worksheet takes another six minutes. The customer's hold lasts twenty-four minutes.

Assume every other deal figure stays fixed. The extra one thousand dollars for the trade comes out of the expected gross profit. The customer's waiting time has no dollar cost assigned in this example.

Before Monday opening, write the approval rule and name a backup for the general manager. The same desk manager follows the request until finance accepts the approved worksheet.

Use a message the manager can answer. The trade appraisal is seventeen thousand dollars. The customer was quoted eighteen thousand dollars. My limit is seventeen thousand five hundred dollars. Please approve the customer's quoted figure or return a figure I can give them. Finance is waiting. Please answer within five minutes.

Five minutes is a trial target. Measure actual reply times. Each over-limit worksheet should carry its written approval. Count worksheets that finance sends back. Count each deal once, and record why the worksheet came back.

On Monday, review the first week's reply times with the desk manager. Open one packet finance sent back and fix its missing field before the next customer arrives.

nextWatch.title: Read the slowest request on Monday
paragraphs: Give the desk manager the week's log before opening. Read the slowest request with the person who had to answer it. If that person had no named backup, put the backup on next week's schedule.
Open one worksheet F&I returned. Fix the missing field with the desk manager, then check the next packet.
